# AthenaK stellar Rosseland opacity table, log10 kappa_R [cm^2/g] on (log10 T[K], log10 rho[g/cm3]); INCLUDES electron scattering
# GS98 metals, X=0.360 Y=0.620 Z=0.020 (AG Car surface, Groh+2009 Table 4); mixture tables/mixture_x0.36_z0.02.txt (TOPS number fractions; AESOPUS/Ferguson GS98 scaled solar, same mixture)
# EXTENDED table (agcar/tables_ext, 10-09). Built by tables_ext/scripts/build_ext.py fergR
# HIGH T: LANL TOPS/ATOMIC (fetch_tops.py, T 0.0005-1 keV, rho 1e-21..1); its data are flat (clamped) below a T-dependent floor (log rho -15.6 at 5800 K, -14 at 1e5 K, -12.4 at 1.1 MK, -11.2 at 8 MK; there the old table values (clamped, kept bitwise) fill -14..floor)
# BLEND: linear in log T of log10 kappa over log T 4.00..4.20 (low-T source below, TOPS above); log T >= 4.20 and log rho >= -14 are BITWISE the old table (tables/*_tops_*)
# LOW-RHO EXTENSION below each source floor: Rosseland = Saha e-scattering + absorption x (rho/rho_e)^s; Planck = kP_e (rho/rho_e)^s; s = local log slope over 0.6 dex, clamped [0,1], boxcar-averaged over +-0.1 dex in log T (see build_ext.py)
# ext2 = FERGUSON PAIR: low-T Rosseland AND Planck from Ferguson et al. 2005 GS98 (f05.gs98.tar.gz md5 96a1b1db, f05.g98.pl.tar.gz md5 69d8b6d3, Wichita State), interpolated as data/stellar_opac/planck_tools/convert_ferguson.py (bilinear in log T, log R); grains included (only below ~2000 K, under both tfloors)
# LOW T (Rosseland): Ferguson et al. 2005 Rosseland g98.35.02 and g98.5.02 (GS98, grains included as in the Planck pair), linear in X to 0.36 (w=0.0667); valid log T 2.70..4.50, log R -8.0..1.0 (R = rho/T6^3)
# VALID BOX (data): log T 2.70..7.065 [Ferguson below log T 4.2, TOPS above 4.0, blended between]; log rho >= TOPS floor (log T >= 4.0) or log R >= -8 (log T < 4.0); below: the physical extension (model, not data); log T > 7.065, log T < 2.70 and log R > 1 (log T < 4.0) EDGE-FILLED
# Read with he_opac_table (he_star_m1), same format as before.
# grid: nT nD lTmin dlT lDmin dlD
# 217 421 2.6 0.025 -21 0.05
# then nT*nD rows, T slowest: log10 kappa [cm^2/g]
